title: Trace a production signal before choosing a response
description: Switch between fleet averages, cohort slices, and versioned traces, then choose whether to continue, pause, or roll back. The same top-line metric can justify different actions once the affected path is visible.

stages.label: Request and cohort
stages.responsibility: Record task, language, tenant, risk class, and experiment assignment.

stages.label: Prompt and model route
stages.responsibility: Attach prompt, model, decoding, policy, and feature-flag versions.

stages.label: Retrieval and tools
stages.responsibility: Track index, corpus, tool, cache, and dependency versions.

stages.label: Output and outcome
stages.responsibility: Join quality, safety, latency, cost, feedback, and delayed task outcome.

scenarios.label: Stable average, damaged cohort
scenarios.detail: Fleet quality looks flat, but Spanish retrieval answers lose fresh citations.
scenarios.recommendation: Roll back the retrieval index version for the affected route, retain the failing traces, and replay them against a repaired snapshot before resuming the canary.

aggregate.headline: The fleet average appears inside its normal band
aggregate.detail: Healthy English traffic dominates the aggregate, so the affected cohort contributes too little weight to trigger a global quality alert.
aggregate.suspect: No component can be isolated from an aggregate-only result.

slice.headline: Spanish retrieval quality crosses the abort threshold
slice.detail: The regression is concentrated in citation freshness and starts at the candidate experiment boundary, which rules out a fleet-wide model shift.
slice.suspect: The affected experiment route or one of its versioned dependencies.

trace.headline: A stale Spanish index snapshot caused unsupported answers
trace.detail: Failing traces share the candidate route and retrieval-index es-2026-07-18; the prompt and model versions match healthy control traces.
trace.suspect: The candidate retrieval snapshot is missing the latest Spanish source documents.

scenarios.label: Latency rises without quality loss
scenarios.detail: A model-provider route throttles long requests while answers remain correct.
scenarios.recommendation: Pause expansion, route long-context traffic to the healthy provider, and verify queue and timeout recovery before changing model quality gates.

aggregate.headline: Latency and timeout signals rise together
aggregate.detail: The fleet view establishes operational pressure but cannot show whether the model, scheduler, or provider route is responsible.

slice.headline: Only long-context requests breach the latency budget
slice.detail: Short requests and output quality remain stable, narrowing the incident to a capacity or route-specific problem.
slice.suspect: The long-context serving route or its provider capacity.

trace.headline: Provider throttling stretches queue and first-token time
trace.detail: Trace joins show the candidate provider route returning throttle metadata before timeout growth; model outputs that finish still pass quality checks.
trace.suspect: The candidate provider route lacks reserved long-context capacity.

scenarios.label: Feedback spike without corroboration
scenarios.detail: Thumbs-down events rise after a UI survey change, but hard outcomes stay healthy.
scenarios.recommendation: Continue the bounded canary, annotate the feedback-instrument change, and recalibrate the complaint baseline before treating the spike as a model regression.

aggregate.headline: A complaint spike is visible, but the model signal is ambiguous
aggregate.detail: Feedback changed while quality, safety, completion, latency, and errors stayed inside their declared bands.
aggregate.suspect: Either model behavior or the feedback collection path changed.

slice.headline: The spike follows survey exposure, not model assignment
slice.detail: Control and candidate traffic show the same increase when the new survey is visible, weakening the model-regression hypothesis.
slice.suspect: The outcome instrument changed independently of model behavior.

trace.headline: A UI event-version change explains the feedback discontinuity
trace.detail: Versioned traces show a new survey prompt doubling response rate for both control and candidate while downstream task outcomes remain stable.
trace.suspect: The feedback instrumentation changed the measurement baseline.
